prerequisites: Knowledge of the fundamentals of machine elements and design theory including CAD
Successful completion of VO Machine Elements 1 (3 ECTS)
Successful completion of VO Machine Elements 2 (3 ECTS)
Successful completion of UE Machine Elements Design Exercise (4 ECTS)
Successful completion of the StEOP (Study Entrance and Orientation Phase)

learning_outcomes.text: Independent design of planetary and bevel gearboxes.
Explaining the functionality of worm, cycloid gearboxes and freewheels.
Independent calculation of gearing microgeometries.
Understanding of gearing damage and its consequences.
Mastery of advanced machine constructions and calculation tasks.
Methodologically sound implementation of machine constructions with 3D-CAD systems.
Application of computer-aided design and verification methods.
Applying common machine element calculation programs.
Explaining the most important cost parameters using the example of gearbox construction.
Understanding the motion sequences and resulting forces in gearboxes with multi-body simulation systems.
To reliably design planetary and bevel gearboxes based on given requirements.
To explain understandably the functionality of worm, cycloid gearboxes, and freewheels with suitable examples.
To correctly calculate gearing microgeometries for specified load and manufacturing conditions.
To professionally describe typical gearing damage and its consequences for load capacity and service life, or to assess underlying damage mechanisms.
To purposefully process advanced machine constructions and calculation-oriented tasks based on relevant standards.
To implement machine constructions using 3D-CAD systems and carry them out methodologically soundly.
To appropriately apply computer-aided design and verification methods for gearbox components and compare the results with legal regulations.
To safely use common machine element calculation programs for design and evaluation.
To clearly identify the most important cost parameters in gearbox construction and, if necessary, implement designs more cost-efficiently.
To systematically analyze motion sequences and resulting forces in gearboxes with multi-body simulation systems.
To already identify possible critical operating conditions derivable from this in the design phase.
To explain and present one's own CAD design in an audience-appropriate manner.
To constructively discuss and compare various CAD design solutions within the framework of peer feedback.
To compare alternatives of design, layout, and simulation strategies based on defined criteria.
To comprehensibly explain one's own derivations, assumptions, and approximation steps.
To identify everyday and work-related application examples.
To distinguish effective behavior in these application contexts from that in an academic setting.

syllabus_topics: Multi-body system dynamic analysis of gearboxes
teaching_methods: Lectures on theoretical foundations and basic calculations of the mentioned contents
Practicing and applying the contents through calculation examples
